### Description

A joint used to ignore collision between two specific bodies.
As a side effect of being a joint, it also keeps the two bodies in the same simulation island meaning they'll wake/sleep at the same time and be solved together on the same thread.

### Properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [bodyA](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-bodyA.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-bodyA.html") | The first body the joint constrains. |
| [bodyB](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-bodyB.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-bodyB.html") | The second body the joint constrains. |
| [callbackTarget](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-callbackTarget.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-callbackTarget.html") | Get/Set the Object that event callbacks for this joint will be sent to. Care should be taken with any Object assigned as a callback target that isn't a Object as this assignment will not in itself keep the object alive and can be garbage collected. To avoid this, you should have at least a single reference to the object in your code. To remove the object assigned here, set the callback target to NULL. This includes the following events: - A JointThresholdEvent with call IJointThresholdCallback. |
| [collideConnected](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-collideConnected.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-collideConnected.html") | This is unused in this specific joint and is always false. Typically this gets whether the shapes on the pair of bodies can come into contact. |
| [currentAngularSeparationError](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-currentAngularSeparationError.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-currentAngularSeparationError.html") | This is unused in this specific joint. Typically this would get the current angular separation error for this joint. |
| [currentConstraintForce](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-currentConstraintForce.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-currentConstraintForce.html") | This is unused in this specific joint. Typically this would get the current constraint force used by the joint, usually in newtons. |
| [currentConstraintTorque](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-currentConstraintTorque.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-currentConstraintTorque.html") | This is unused in this specific joint. Typically this would get the current constraint torque used by the joint, usually in newton-meters. |
| [currentLinearSeparationError](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-currentLinearSeparationError.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-currentLinearSeparationError.html") | This is unused in this specific joint. Typically this would get the current linear separation error for this joint. |
| [definition](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-definition.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-definition.html") | Get or set the joint definition. Reading returns the joint's current configuration, including PhysicsIgnoreJoint.bodyA and PhysicsIgnoreJoint.bodyB. Writing applies every configurable property in place but does not change the connected bodies, which are fixed when the joint is created. |
| [drawScale](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-drawScale.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-drawScale.html") | This is unused in this specific joint. Typically this would control the scaling of the joint drawing. |
| [forceThreshold](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-forceThreshold.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-forceThreshold.html") | This is unused in this specific joint. Typically this is the force threshold beyond which a joint event will be produced. |
| [isOwned](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-isOwned.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-isOwned.html") | Get if the joint is owned. See PhysicsJoint.SetOwner. |
| [isValid](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-isValid.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-isValid.html") | Checks if the joint is valid. |
| [jointType](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-jointType.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-jointType.html") | Gets the joint type. See JointType. |
| [localAnchorA](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-localAnchorA.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-localAnchorA.html") | This is unused in this specific joint. Typically this is the local anchor frame constraint relative to bodyA's origin. |
| [localAnchorB](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-localAnchorB.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-localAnchorB.html") | This is unused in this specific joint. Typically this is the local anchor frame constraint relative to bodyB's origin. |
| [ownerUserData](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-ownerUserData.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-ownerUserData.html") | Get PhysicsUserData that can be used for any purpose, typically by the owner only. |
| [physicsHandle](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-physicsHandle.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-physicsHandle.html") | Get the physics handle. |
| [torqueThreshold](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-torqueThreshold.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-torqueThreshold.html") | This is unused in this specific joint. Typically this is the torque threshold beyond which a joint event will be produced. |
| [tuningDamping](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-tuningDamping.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-tuningDamping.html") | This is unused in this specific joint. Typically this would control the joint stiffness damping, non-dimensional. Use 1 for critical damping. |
| [tuningFrequency](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-tuningFrequency.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-tuningFrequency.html") | This is unused in this specific joint. Typically this would control the joint stiffness frequency, in cycles per second. |
| [userData](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-userData.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-userData.html") | Get/Set PhysicsUserData that can be used for any purpose. The physics system doesn't use this data, it is entirely for custom use. |
| [world](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-world.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-world.html") | Get the world the body is attached to. |
| [worldDrawing](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-worldDrawing.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-worldDrawing.html") | Controls whether this joint is automatically drawn when the world is drawn. |

### Constructors

| Constructor | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [PhysicsIgnoreJoint](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-ctor.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-ctor.html") | Create a joint from a physics handle. NOTE: You must ensure that the physics handle represents the correct object type otherwise hard to detect bugs can occur. |

### Public Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Destroy](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint.Destroy.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint.Destroy.html") | Destroy the joint. If the object is owned with PhysicsJoint.SetOwner then you must provide the owner key it returned. Failing to do so will return a warning and the joint will not be destroyed. |
| [Draw](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint.Draw.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint.Draw.html") | Draw a PhysicsJoint that visually represents its current state in the world. |
| [GetOwner](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint.GetOwner.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint.GetOwner.html") | Get the owner object associated with this joint as specified using PhysicsJoint.SetOwner. |
| [SetOwner](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint.SetOwner.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint.SetOwner.html") | Set the (optional) owner object associated with this joint and return an owner key that must be specified when destroying the joint with PhysicsJoint.Destroy. The physics system provides access to all objects, including the ability to destroy them so this feature can be used to stop accidental destruction of objects that are owned by other objects. You can only set the owner once, multiple attempts will produce a warning. The lifetime of the specified owner object is not linked to this joint i.e. this joint will still be owned by the owner object, even if it is destroyed. It is also valid to not specify an owner object (NULL) to simply gain an owner key however it can be useful, if simply for debugging purposes and discovery, to know which object is the owner. |
| [SetOwnerUserData](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint.SetOwnerUserData.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint.SetOwnerUserData.html") | Set PhysicsUserData that can be used for any purpose, typically by the owner only. |
| [WakeBodies](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint.WakeBodies.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint.WakeBodies.html") | Wake the pair of bodies the joint is constraining. |

### Static Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Create](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint.Create.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint.Create.html") | Create a PhysicsIgnoreJoint in the specified world. |
| [DestroyBatch](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint.DestroyBatch.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint.DestroyBatch.html") | Destroy a batch of joints. Owned joints will produce a warning and will not be destroyed (see PhysicsJoint.SetOwner). Any invalid joints will be ignored. |

### Operators

| Operator | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [PhysicsIgnoreJoint](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-operator_PhysicsJoint.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-operator_PhysicsJoint.html") | Cast to a PhysicsIgnoreJoint from the base PhysicsJoint. The provided joint must be a joint type of PhysicsJoint.JointType.IgnoreJoint. |
| [PhysicsJoint](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-operator_PhysicsIgnoreJoint.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint-operator_PhysicsIgnoreJoint.html") | Cast to the base PhysicsJoint. |

## Declaration

public bool Equals(Object other);

### Description

Returns true if the given vector is exactly equal to this vector.

Due to floating point inaccuracies, this might return false for vectors which are essentially (but not exactly) equal. Use the [== operator](Vector3-operator_eq.html "Vector3-operator_eq.html") to test two vectors for approximate equality.

## Declaration

public static void\* MallocTracked(long size,
int alignment,
[Allocator](Unity.Collections.Allocator.html "Unity.Collections.Allocator.html") allocator,
int callstacksToSkip);

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| size | The size of the memory block to allocate, in bytes. Ensure the size is sufficient for the intended data storage to avoid buffer overflow. |
| alignment | Specifies the alignment of the memory block. Alignment must be a power of two to ensure efficient memory access patterns for various processor architectures. |
| allocator | The memory allocator used to manage the allocation. Choose an allocator type that matches the intended use case for the allocated memory, such as [Allocator.Temp](Unity.Collections.Allocator.Temp.html "Unity.Collections.Allocator.Temp.html") or [Allocator.Persistent](Unity.Collections.Allocator.Persistent.html "Unity.Collections.Allocator.Persistent.html"). |
| callstacksToSkip | Specifies the number of call stack frames to skip when tracking memory. Adjust this to refine the granularity of stack traces collected for memory profiling. |

### Returns

**void\***
A pointer to the allocated memory block. Manage this pointer diligently, ensuring it is freed appropriately to prevent memory leaks and accessing invalid memory.

### Description

Allocates a block of memory with specified size, alignment, and tracking information.

The `MallocTracked` method allocates memory while providing options to track memory allocations for debugging and profiling purposes. This function is similar to [UnsafeUtility.Malloc](Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.Malloc.html "Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.Malloc.html"), but with additional tracking that helps identify memory allocations that might contribute to memory leaks or inefficiencies in performance-critical applications.  
  
Ensure that the allocated memory is properly freed with [UnsafeUtility.Free](Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.Free.html "Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.Free.html") when it is no longer required to avoid memory leaks. Balance the `callstacksToSkip` parameter value to focus on your debugging needs while minimizing overhead.

```
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
using Unity.Collections;
using Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe;
using UnityEngine;  
  
public class MallocTrackedSimplifiedExample : MonoBehaviour
{
    void Start()
    {
        // Enable Native Leak Detection with stack trace for debugging
        UnsafeUtility.SetLeakDetectionMode(NativeLeakDetectionMode.EnabledWithStackTrace);
        
        // Allocate a block of memory for a CustomNativeArray
        Allocate(10, Allocator.Persistent, out CustomNativeArray<int> array);  
  
        // NOTE: Not freeing the buffer in this example; this is intentional for demonstration.
        // During a Domain reload, such as entering/exiting Play Mode, a warning will appear
        // if memory is not properly freed, aiding in identifying leaks.
    }  
  
    [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)]
    unsafe struct CustomNativeArray<T> where T : struct
    {
        public void* m_Buffer;
        public int m_Length;
        public Allocator m_AllocatorLabel;
    }  
  
    static void Allocate<T>(int length, Allocator allocator, out CustomNativeArray<T> array) where T : struct
    {
        long totalSize = UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>() * length;
        array = default;  
  
        unsafe
        {
            // Allocate memory with leak detection tracking
            array.m_Buffer = UnsafeUtility.MallocTracked(totalSize, UnsafeUtility.AlignOf<T>(), allocator, 0);
        }  
  
        // Set the array metadata
        array.m_Length = length;
        array.m_AllocatorLabel = allocator;
    }
}
```

See Also: [UnsafeUtility.FreeTracked](Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.FreeTracked.html "Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.FreeTracked.html"), [UnsafeUtility.Malloc](Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.Malloc.html "Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.Malloc.html"), [UnsafeUtility.SetLeakDetectionMode](Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.SetLeakDetectionMode.html "Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.SetLeakDetectionMode.html").

---

## Declaration

public static void\* MallocTracked(long size,
int alignment,
[MemoryLabel](Unity.Collections.MemoryLabel.html "Unity.Collections.MemoryLabel.html") label,
int callstacksToSkip);

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| size | The size of the memory block to allocate, in bytes. Ensure the size is sufficient for the intended data storage to avoid buffer overflow. |
| alignment | Specifies the alignment of the memory block. Alignment must be a power of two to ensure efficient memory access patterns for various processor architectures. |
| label | The memory label to allocate under. |
| callstacksToSkip | Specifies the number of call stack frames to skip when tracking memory. Adjust this to refine the granularity of stack traces collected for memory profiling. |

### Returns

**void\***
A pointer to the allocated memory block. Manage this pointer carefully to prevent memory leaks and ensure proper deallocation.

### Description

Allocates a block of memory with specified size, alignment, memory label and tracking information.

The `MallocTracked` method allocates memory while providing options to track memory allocations for debugging and profiling purposes. This function is similar to [UnsafeUtility.Malloc](Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.Malloc.html "Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.Malloc.html"), but with additional tracking that helps identify memory allocations that might contribute to memory leaks or inefficiencies in performance-critical applications.  
  
Specifying a memory label helps in profiling and debugging memory usage in Unity.  
  
To avoid memory leaks, free the allocated memory with [UnsafeUtility.Free](Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.Free.html "Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.Free.html") when it's no longer required. Balance the `callstacksToSkip` parameter value to focus on your debugging needs while minimizing overhead.

See Also: Unity.Collections.MemoryLabel, [UnsafeUtility.FreeTracked](Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.FreeTracked.html "Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.FreeTracked.html"), [UnsafeUtility.Malloc](Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.Malloc.html "Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.Malloc.html"), [UnsafeUtility.SetLeakDetectionMode](Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.SetLeakDetectionMode.html "Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe.UnsafeUtility.SetLeakDetectionMode.html").

public string Tooltip;

### Description

The tooltip text displayed when hovering over the module in the Profiler window.

Provides additional information about the module's purpose and functionality. This property is optional and can be set using object initialization syntax.

```
using System;
using Unity.Profiling;
using Unity.Profiling.Editor;  
  
[ProfilerModuleMetadataAttribute(
    "Memory Allocation Tracker",
    Tooltip = "Tracks memory allocations and garbage collection activity per frame"
)]
public class MemoryAllocationProfilerModule : ProfilerModule
{
    static readonly ProfilerCounterDescriptor[] k_ChartCounters = new ProfilerCounterDescriptor[]
    {
        new ProfilerCounterDescriptor("Total Allocations", ProfilerCategory.Memory),
        new ProfilerCounterDescriptor("GC Allocations", ProfilerCategory.Memory),
    };  
  
    public MemoryAllocationProfilerModule() : base(k_ChartCounters) {}
}
```

Additional resources: [ProfilerModuleMetadataAttribute](Unity.Profiling.Editor.ProfilerModuleMetadataAttribute.html "Unity.Profiling.Editor.ProfilerModuleMetadataAttribute.html"), [ProfilerModule](Unity.Profiling.Editor.ProfilerModule.html "Unity.Profiling.Editor.ProfilerModule.html").

[Switch to Manual](../Manual/class-LightingSettings.html "Go to LightingSettings Component in the Manual")

public float filteringAtrousPositionSigmaAO;

### Description

Specifies the threshold the Progressive Lightmapper uses to filter direct light stored in the lightmap when using the A-Trous filter. (Editor only).

The range is 0 through 2. The default value is 0.5. A higher value will increase the threshold, which reduces the amount of noise in the direct lighting component of the lightmap. Too high of a value can cause a loss of detail in the lightmap.  
  
This setting affects lightmaps generated by the Baked Global Illumination system. It only applies to the the Progressive Lightmapper.  
  
When Unity serializes this `LightingSettings` object as a [Lighting Settings Asset](../Manual/class-LightingSettings.html "../Manual/class-LightingSettings.html"), this property corresponds to the **Filtering > Direct Filter > Sigma** property in the Lighting Settings Asset Inspector.  
  
Additional resources: [Lighting Settings Asset](../Manual/class-LightingSettings.html "../Manual/class-LightingSettings.html").

[Switch to Manual](../Manual/class-Transform.html "Go to Transform Component in the Manual")

public [Vector3](Vector3.html "Vector3.html") localPosition;

### Description

Position of the transform relative to the parent transform.

If the transform has no parent, it's the same as [Transform.position](Transform-position.html "Transform-position.html").  
  
Like most Transform operations, localPosition may not always be accessible, particularly during certain operations such as an [Undo](Undo.html "Undo.html") operation or before the transform hierarchy is fully initialized. For example, OnValidate() can be invoked before the hierarchy is completely set up, potentially causing a logged error. If you attempt to access localPosition at an incompatible time, it will return Vector3.zero instead of the actual value.

```
using UnityEngine;
using System.Collections;  
  
public class ExampleClass : MonoBehaviour
{
    void Example()
    {
        // Move the object to the same position as the parent:
        transform.localPosition = new Vector3(0, 0, 0);  
  
        // Get the y component of the position relative to the parent
        // and print it to the Console
        print(transform.localPosition.y);
    }
}
```

Note that the parent transform's world rotation and scale are applied to the local position when calculating the world position.
This means that while 1 unit in [Transform.position](Transform-position.html "Transform-position.html") is always 1 unit, 1 unit in [Transform.localPosition](Transform-localPosition.html "Transform-localPosition.html") will get scaled by the scale of all ancestors.

public [ParticleSystem](ParticleSystem.html "ParticleSystem.html") collision0;

### Description

Sub-Particle System which spawns at the locations of the collision of the particles from the parent system.

This module's Particle System uses the first set of emission burst properties to spawn a sub-Particle System. If the system does not contain burst properties, then the system emits nothing; if the system contains more than one set of burst properties, then it ignores the additional properties.

## Declaration

## Declaration

public static void LoadPrefabContentsIntoPreviewScene(string prefabPath,
[Scene](SceneManagement.Scene.html "SceneManagement.Scene.html") scene,
out GameObject rootGameObject);

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| scene | The Scene to load the contents into. |
| prefabPath | The path of the Prefab Asset to load the contents of. |
| rootGameObject | The root GameObject of the loaded Prefab Asset or null if the Prefab couldn't be loaded. |

### Description

Loads a Prefab Asset at a given path into a given preview scene.

You can use this to get the content of the Prefab and modify it directly instead of going through an instance of the Prefab. This is useful for batch operations.  
  
Once you have modified the Prefab you have to write it back using [SaveAsPrefabAsset](PrefabUtility.SaveAsPrefabAsset.html "PrefabUtility.SaveAsPrefabAsset.html"). After that you can either reuse your preview scene for other purposes, or close the preview scene with [EditorSceneManager.CloseScene](SceneManagement.EditorSceneManager.CloseScene.html "SceneManagement.EditorSceneManager.CloseScene.html").

Additional resources: [DragAndDrop](DragAndDrop.html "DragAndDrop.html") class.

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [None](DragAndDropVisualMode.None.html "DragAndDropVisualMode.None.html") | No indication (drag should not be performed). |
| [Copy](DragAndDropVisualMode.Copy.html "DragAndDropVisualMode.Copy.html") | Copy dragged objects. |
| [Link](DragAndDropVisualMode.Link.html "DragAndDropVisualMode.Link.html") | Link dragged objects to target. |
| [Move](DragAndDropVisualMode.Move.html "DragAndDropVisualMode.Move.html") | Move dragged objects. |
| [Generic](DragAndDropVisualMode.Generic.html "DragAndDropVisualMode.Generic.html") | Generic drag operation. |
| [Rejected](DragAndDropVisualMode.Rejected.html "DragAndDropVisualMode.Rejected.html") | Rejected drag operation. |

public [GraphicsBuffer](GraphicsBuffer.html "GraphicsBuffer.html") vertexBuffer;

### Description

The vertex buffer that Unity uses to define geometries used by ray tracing instances.

Define the vertex buffer format by specifiying a list of vertex attributes in [vertexAttributes](Rendering.RayTracingMultiGeometryInstanceConfig-vertexAttributes.html "Rendering.RayTracingMultiGeometryInstanceConfig-vertexAttributes.html") array.   
  
You can use a common vertex buffer as a pool to define multiple geometries used by ray tracing instances that have different properties (for example different materials).  
  
Specify `GraphicsBuffer.Target.Raw` for the GraphicsBuffer.Target parameter when creating the vertex buffer from scripts. If the buffer is also used in rasterization then add the `GraphicsBuffer.Target.Vertex` flag.

public static [Vector3](Vector3.html "Vector3.html") gravity;

### Description

The gravity applied to all rigid bodies in the Scene.

Gravity can be turned off for an individual rigidbody using its [Rigidbody.useGravity](Rigidbody-useGravity.html "Rigidbody-useGravity.html") property.

```
using UnityEngine;
using System.Collections;  
  
public class ExampleClass : MonoBehaviour
{
    void Example()
    {
        Physics.gravity = new Vector3(0, -1.0F, 0);
    }
}
```

ParticleSystem.gravityModifiers is Obsolete.

This is similar to [bandwidth](Unity.IO.LowLevel.Unsafe.AsyncReadManagerSummaryMetrics-bandwidth.html "Unity.IO.LowLevel.Unsafe.AsyncReadManagerSummaryMetrics-bandwidth.html"), but takes into account the waiting time as well as reading time.

## Declaration

public void DrawRenderer([Renderer](Renderer.html "Renderer.html") renderer,
[Material](Material.html "Material.html") material,
int submeshIndex = 0,
int shaderPass = -1);

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| renderer | Renderer to draw. |
| material | Material to use. |
| submeshIndex | Which subset of the mesh to render. |
| shaderPass | Which pass of the shader to use (default is -1, which renders all passes). |

### Description

Add a "draw renderer" command.

Note that the rendered mesh will not have any lighting related shader data (light colors, directions, shadows, light and reflection probes etc.) set up. If the shader used by the material uses any lighting related variables, the results are undefined.  
  
Additional resources: [DrawMesh](Rendering.CommandBuffer.DrawMesh.html "Rendering.CommandBuffer.DrawMesh.html").

### Description

An event produced by a pair of Shapes, neither of which are a trigger, began touching.
The shapes provided may have been destroyed so they should always be validated with [PhysicsShape.isValid](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape-isValid.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape-isValid.html").
See [PhysicsWorld.contactBeginEvents](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactBeginEvents.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld-contactBeginEvents.html").

### Properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [contactId](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.ContactBeginEvent-contactId.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.ContactBeginEvent-contactId.html") | The unique Id of the contact. This contact is volatile and may be destroyed automatically when the world is modified or simulated therefore it should always be checked for validity with PhysicsShape.ContactId.isValid. |
| [shapeA](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.ContactBeginEvent-shapeA.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.ContactBeginEvent-shapeA.html") | One of the shapes involved in the event. |
| [shapeB](Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.ContactBeginEvent-shapeB.html "Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.ContactBeginEvent-shapeB.html") | The other shape involved in the event. |

[Switch to Manual](../Manual/class-ParticleSystem.html "Go to ParticleSystem Component in the Manual")

public float yMultiplier;

### Description

Defines the y-axis multiplier.

Changing this property is more efficient than accessing the entire curve, if you only want to change the overall y-axis multiplier.

```
using UnityEngine;
using System.Collections;  
  
[RequireComponent(typeof(ParticleSystem))]
public class ExampleClass : MonoBehaviour
{
    private ParticleSystem ps;
    public bool moduleEnabled = true;
    public float hSliderValue = 10.0f;  
  
    void Start()
    {
        ps = GetComponent<ParticleSystem>();
    }  
  
    void Update()
    {
        var forceOverLifetime = ps.forceOverLifetime;
        forceOverLifetime.enabled = moduleEnabled;
        forceOverLifetime.yMultiplier = hSliderValue;
    }  
  
    void OnGUI()
    {
        moduleEnabled = GUI.Toggle(new Rect(25, 45, 100, 30), moduleEnabled, "Enabled");
        hSliderValue = GUI.HorizontalSlider(new Rect(25, 85, 100, 30), hSliderValue, -50.0f, 50.0f);
    }
}
```

Is something described here not working as you expect it to? It might be a **Known Issue**. Please check with the Issue Tracker at

# TransformSceneHandle

struct in
UnityEngine.Animations

Your email

Submit suggestion

Cancel

### Description

Handle to read position, rotation and scale of an object in the Scene.

TransformSceneHandle are read-only.  
  
A TransformSceneHandle is a safe handle on a [TransformAccess](Jobs.TransformAccess.html "Jobs.TransformAccess.html"). The [Animator](Animator.html "Animator.html") used to create this handle manages the validity of this handle.

```
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEngine.Playables;
using UnityEngine.Animations;  
  
public struct TransformSceneHandleJob : IAnimationJob
{
    public TransformSceneHandle handle;  
  
    public void ProcessRootMotion(AnimationStream stream)
    {
        // Log the local position.
        var position = handle.GetLocalPosition(stream);
        Debug.LogFormat("Position: {0}", position);  
  
        // Log the local rotation (converted from euler).
        var rotation = handle.GetLocalRotation(stream);
        Debug.LogFormat("Rotation: {0}", rotation.eulerAngles);  
  
        // Log the local scale.
        var scale = handle.GetLocalScale(stream);
        Debug.LogFormat("Scale: {0}", scale);
    }  
  
    public void ProcessAnimation(AnimationStream stream)
    {
    }
}  
  
[RequireComponent(typeof(Animator))]
public class TransformSceneHandleExample : MonoBehaviour
{
    public Transform sceneTransform;  
  
    PlayableGraph m_Graph;
    AnimationScriptPlayable m_AnimationScriptPlayable;  
  
    void Start()
    {
        if (sceneTransform == null)
            return;  
  
        var animator = GetComponent<Animator>();  
  
        m_Graph = PlayableGraph.Create("TransformSceneHandleExample");
        var output = AnimationPlayableOutput.Create(m_Graph, "output", animator);  
  
        var animationJob = new TransformSceneHandleJob();
        animationJob.handle = animator.BindSceneTransform(sceneTransform);
        m_AnimationScriptPlayable = AnimationScriptPlayable.Create(m_Graph, animationJob);  
  
        output.SetSourcePlayable(m_AnimationScriptPlayable);
        m_Graph.Play();
    }  
  
    void OnDisable()
    {
        if (sceneTransform == null)
            return;  
  
        m_Graph.Destroy();
    }
}
```

Additional resources: [AnimatorJobExtensions.BindSceneTransform](Animations.AnimatorJobExtensions.BindSceneTransform.html "Animations.AnimatorJobExtensions.BindSceneTransform.html"), [PropertySceneHandle](Animations.PropertySceneHandle.html "Animations.PropertySceneHandle.html"), [PropertyStreamHandle](Animations.PropertyStreamHandle.html "Animations.PropertyStreamHandle.html"), and [TransformStreamHandle](Animations.TransformStreamHandle.html "Animations.TransformStreamHandle.html").

### Public Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [GetGlobalTR](Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetGlobalTR.html "Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetGlobalTR.html") | Gets the position and scaled rotation of the transform in world space. |
| [GetLocalPosition](Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetLocalPosition.html "Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetLocalPosition.html") | Gets the position of the transform relative to the parent. |
| [GetLocalRotation](Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetLocalRotation.html "Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetLocalRotation.html") | Gets the rotation of the transform relative to the parent. |
| [GetLocalScale](Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetLocalScale.html "Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetLocalScale.html") | Gets the scale of the transform relative to the parent. |
| [GetLocalToParentMatrix](Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetLocalToParentMatrix.html "Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetLocalToParentMatrix.html") | Gets the local to parent matrix of the transform. |
| [GetLocalToWorldMatrix](Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetLocalToWorldMatrix.html "Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetLocalToWorldMatrix.html") | Gets the local to world matrix of the transform. |
| [GetLocalTRS](Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetLocalTRS.html "Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetLocalTRS.html") | Gets the position, rotation and scale of the transform relative to the parent. |
| [GetPosition](Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetPosition.html "Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetPosition.html") | Gets the position of the transform in world space. |
| [GetRotation](Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetRotation.html "Animations.TransformSceneHandle.GetRotation.html") | Gets the rotation of the transform in world space. |
| [IsValid](Animations.TransformSceneHandle.IsValid.html "Animations.TransformSceneHandle.IsValid.html") | Returns whether this is a valid handle. |

## Declaration

public static [Plane](Unity.Mathematics.Geometry.Plane.html "Unity.Mathematics.Geometry.Plane.html") CreateFromUnitNormalAndPointInPlane([float3](Unity.Mathematics.float3.html "Unity.Mathematics.float3.html") unitNormal,
[float3](Unity.Mathematics.float3.html "Unity.Mathematics.float3.html") pointInPlane);

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| unitNormal | A non-zero vector that is perpendicular to the plane. It must be unit length. |
| pointInPlane | A point that lies in the plane. |

### Returns

**Plane**
Normalized Plane constructed from given inputs.

### Description

Creates a normalized Plane without normalization cost.

If you have a unit length normal vector, you can create a Plane faster than using one of its constructors
by calling this function.

| --- | --- |
| positions | An array that stores the location of 3d positions. |
| transform | A matrix that changes the position, rotation and size of the bounds calculation. |

### Returns

**Bounds**
Calculates the axis-aligned bounding box.

### Description

Calculates the bounding box from the given array of [positions](GeometryUtility-positions.html "GeometryUtility-positions.html") and the transformation matrix.

[GeometryUtility.CalculateBounds](GeometryUtility.CalculateBounds.html "GeometryUtility.CalculateBounds.html") generates a [Bounds](Bounds.html "Bounds.html") bounding box. The positions parameter stores a 3d point array. Each point is inside the generated axis-aligned bounding box. The transform parameter provides a transformation [Matrix4x4](Matrix4x4.html "Matrix4x4.html") that uses a Vector3 position, Quaternion rotation, and Vector3 scale.  
  
The example below shows how to use [CalculateBounds](GeometryUtility.CalculateBounds.html "GeometryUtility.CalculateBounds.html"). A [LightProbeGroup](LightProbeGroup.html "LightProbeGroup.html") passes [positions](GeometryUtility-positions.html "GeometryUtility-positions.html") into [CalculateBounds](GeometryUtility.CalculateBounds.html "GeometryUtility.CalculateBounds.html"). The example code creates a bounding box with eight Light Probes. By default, the Light Probes are one unit from each corner of a unit cube.  
  
To run the example:

1. Create a Project and add an empty [GameObject](GameObject.html "GameObject.html") called `GameObject`.
2. Add a 3D cube as a child of `GameObject` and call it `Cube`.
3. Add a [LightProbeGroup](LightProbeGroup.html "LightProbeGroup.html") component to `Cube`.
4. Add the script below to `Cube`.
5. Run the `Project` and switch back to the `Scene` view.

In the `Scene` view, you can see the [LightProbeGroup](LightProbeGroup.html "LightProbeGroup.html"). When the game runs, the rotation changes in `Awake`. The eight yellow spheres that indicate the [LightProbeGroup](LightProbeGroup.html "LightProbeGroup.html") change position and the Cube appears rotated. `Scene` mode shows the `Cube` rotated in the x, y and z axes, and shows in the `Local tool handle`. Rotating the `Cube` changes the positions of the eight [LightProbeGroup](LightProbeGroup.html "LightProbeGroup.html") Light Probes. The `Scene` mode rotates and zooms to show the Light Probes. Also, the `Cube` rotates and the [LightProbeGroup](LightProbeGroup.html "LightProbeGroup.html") updates. If you rescale the `Cube`, the [LightProbeGroup](LightProbeGroup.html "LightProbeGroup.html") changes size.

```
using UnityEngine;
using System.Collections;  
  
// GeometryUtility.CalculateBounds - example  
  
public class Example : MonoBehaviour
{
    void Awake()
    {
        transform.position = new Vector3(0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
        transform.Rotate(10.0f, 30.0f, -50.0f, Space.Self);  
  
        Debug.Log(transform.localToWorldMatrix);
    }  
  
    void OnDrawGizmosSelected()
    {
        LightProbeGroup lightProbeGroup = GetComponent<LightProbeGroup>();  
  
        Vector3 center = transform.position;
        Bounds bounds = GeometryUtility.CalculateBounds(lightProbeGroup.probePositions, transform.localToWorldMatrix);
        Gizmos.color = new Color(1, 1, 1, 0.25f);
        Gizmos.DrawCube(center, bounds.size);
        Gizmos.DrawWireCube(center, bounds.size);
    }
}
```

### Description

Representation of RGBA colors.

This structure is used throughout Unity to pass colors around.
Each color component is a floating point value with a range from 0 to 1.  
  
Components ([r](Color-r.html "Color-r.html"),[g](Color-g.html "Color-g.html"),[b](Color-b.html "Color-b.html")) define a color in RGB color space. Alpha component ([a](Color-a.html "Color-a.html"))
defines transparency - alpha of one is completely opaque, alpha of zero is completely
transparent.

```
using UnityEngine;  
  
public class ColorExample : MonoBehaviour
{
    void Start()
    {
        // Initialize with RGB
        Color redColor = new Color(1f, 0f, 0f);  
  
        // Initialize with RGBA
        Color blueWithAlpha = new Color(0f, 0f, 1f, 0.5f);  
  
        // Initialize with hex
        ColorUtility.TryParseHtmlString("#00FF00", out Color greenFromHex);  
  
        // Initialize with HSV
        float hue = 0.6f;
        float saturation = 0.9f;
        float value = 0.7f;
        Color fromHSV = Color.HSVToRGB(hue, saturation, value);  
  
        // Use some of the preset colors
        Color cornflower = Color.cornflowerBlue;
        Color lawn = Color.lawnGreen;
        Color lemon = Color.lemonChiffon;
        Color violet = Color.violet;  
  
        // Create complementary color
        Color complementary = new Color(
            1f - redColor.r,
            1f - redColor.g,
            1f - redColor.b
        );
        // Lerp between colors
        Color lerpedColor = Color.Lerp(redColor, blueWithAlpha, 0.5f);  
  
        // Darken color
        Color darkercolor = lerpedColor * 0.8f;  
  
        // Lighten color
        Color lighterColor = lerpedColor + Color.white * 0.2f;
    }
}
```

### Properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [a](Color-a.html "Color-a.html") | Alpha component of the color (0 is transparent, 1 is opaque). |
| [b](Color-b.html "Color-b.html") | Blue component of the color. |
| [g](Color-g.html "Color-g.html") | Green component of the color. |
| [gamma](Color-gamma.html "Color-gamma.html") | A version of the color that has had the gamma curve applied. |
| [grayscale](Color-grayscale.html "Color-grayscale.html") | The grayscale value of the color. (Read Only) |
| [linear](Color-linear.html "Color-linear.html") | A color value in linear space converted from an sRGB value. |
| [maxColorComponent](Color-maxColorComponent.html "Color-maxColorComponent.html") | Returns the maximum color component value: Max(r,g,b). |
| [r](Color-r.html "Color-r.html") | Red component of the color. |
| [this[int]](Color.Index_operator.html "Color.Index_operator.html") | Access the r, g, b,a components using [0], [1], [2], [3] respectively. |

### Constructors

| Constructor | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Color](Color-ctor.html "Color-ctor.html") | Constructs a new Color with given r,g,b,a components. |

### Public Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Equals](Color.Equals.html "Color.Equals.html") | Returns true if the given color is exactly equal to this color, i.e. if the red, green, blue, and alpha values are exactly the same. |
| [GetHashCode](Color.GetHashCode.html "Color.GetHashCode.html") | Returns the hash code for this color. This lets you use colors as keys in hash tables. |
| [ToString](Color.ToString.html "Color.ToString.html") | Returns a formatted string of this color. |

### Static Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [HSVToRGB](Color.HSVToRGB.html "Color.HSVToRGB.html") | Creates an RGB colour from HSV input. |
| [Lerp](Color.Lerp.html "Color.Lerp.html") | Linearly interpolates between colors a and b using the interpolation ratio t. |
| [LerpUnclamped](Color.LerpUnclamped.html "Color.LerpUnclamped.html") | Linearly interpolates between colors a and b using the interpolation ratio t. |
| [RGBToHSV](Color.RGBToHSV.html "Color.RGBToHSV.html") | Calculates the hue, saturation and value of an RGB input color. |

### Operators

| Operator | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Color](Color-operator_Vector4.html "Color-operator_Vector4.html") | Colors can be implicitly converted to and from Vector4. |
| [operator -](Color-operator_subtract.html "Color-operator_subtract.html") | Subtracts color b from color a. Each component is subtracted separately. |
| [operator !=](Color-operator_ne.html "Color-operator_ne.html") | Returns true if colors are not equal. |
| [operator \*](Color-operator_multiply.html "Color-operator_multiply.html") | Multiplies two colors together. Each component is multiplied separately. |
| [operator /](Color-operator_divide.html "Color-operator_divide.html") | Divides color a by the float b. Each color component is scaled separately. |
| [operator +](Color-operator_add.html "Color-operator_add.html") | Adds two colors together. Each component is added separately. |
| [operator ==](Color-operator_eq.html "Color-operator_eq.html") | Returns true if two Colors are approximately equal. |
| [Vector4](Color-operator_Color.html "Color-operator_Color.html") | Colors can be implicitly converted to and from Vector4. |

## Declaration

public static [AudioClip](AudioClip.html "AudioClip.html") Start(string deviceName,
bool loop,
int lengthSec,
int frequency);

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| deviceName | The name of the device. |
| loop | Indicates whether the recording should continue recording if lengthSec is reached, and wrap around and record from the beginning of the AudioClip. |
| lengthSec | Is the length of the AudioClip produced by the recording. |
| frequency | The sample rate of the AudioClip produced by the recording. Use [AudioSettings.outputSampleRate](AudioSettings-outputSampleRate.html "AudioSettings-outputSampleRate.html") so the recording matches the project's output sample rate. |

### Returns

**AudioClip**
The function returns null if the recording fails to start.

### Description

Start Recording with device.

If you pass a null or empty string for the device name then the default microphone is used. You can get a list of available microphone devices from the [devices](Microphone-devices.html "Microphone-devices.html") property and the range of sample rates supported by a microphone from the [GetDeviceCaps](Microphone.GetDeviceCaps.html "Microphone.GetDeviceCaps.html") property.

```
using UnityEngine;  
  
public class Example : MonoBehaviour
{
    // Start recording with built-in Microphone and play the recorded audio right away
    void Start()
    {
        AudioSource audioSource = GetComponent<AudioSource>();
        audioSource.clip = Microphone.Start("Built-in Microphone", true, 10, AudioSettings.outputSampleRate);
        audioSource.Play();
    }
}
```

### Description

Use `ProfilerCounterOptions` to specify configuration options when creating a [ProfilerCounter](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.profiling.core@latest/index.html?subfolder=/api/Unity.Profiling.ProfilerCounter-1.html "https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.profiling.core@latest/index.html?subfolder=/api/Unity.Profiling.ProfilerCounter-1.html") or [ProfilerCounterValue](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.profiling.core@latest/index.html?subfolder=/api/Unity.Profiling.ProfilerCounterValue-1.html "https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.profiling.core@latest/index.html?subfolder=/api/Unity.Profiling.ProfilerCounterValue-1.html").

### Properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [None](Unity.Profiling.ProfilerCounterOptions.None.html "Unity.Profiling.ProfilerCounterOptions.None.html") | Specifies no options. |
| [FlushOnEndOfFrame](Unity.Profiling.ProfilerCounterOptions.FlushOnEndOfFrame.html "Unity.Profiling.ProfilerCounterOptions.FlushOnEndOfFrame.html") | Specifies that the counter's current value should be reported to the Unity Profiler every frame. |
| [ResetToZeroOnFlush](Unity.Profiling.ProfilerCounterOptions.ResetToZeroOnFlush.html "Unity.Profiling.ProfilerCounterOptions.ResetToZeroOnFlush.html") | Specifies that the counter's current value should be reset to zero each time it is reported to the Unity Profiler. |

## Declaration

public [AsyncOperation](AsyncOperation.html "AsyncOperation.html") SetTitle(string title);

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| title | The new title for the window. |

### Returns

**AsyncOperation**
An [AsyncOperation](AsyncOperation.html "AsyncOperation.html") that represents the asynchronous operation.

### Description

Sets the title of the window.

```
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEngine.Windowing;  
  
public class SetWindowTitleExample : MonoBehaviour
{
    AsyncOperation asyncOperation = null;  
  
    void Start()
    {
        var window = GameWindow.Main;
        asyncOperation = window.SetTitle("My Game Window");
    }  
  
    void Update()
    {
        if (asyncOperation != null && asyncOperation.isDone)
        {
            Debug.Log("Window title set successfully.");
            asyncOperation = null;
        }
    }
}
```

public float maxDistance;

### Description

The distance where sound either becomes inaudible or stops attenuation, depending on the rolloff mode.

[AudioRolloffMode.Linear](AudioRolloffMode.Linear.html "AudioRolloffMode.Linear.html"): For the linear rolloff mode, the `maxDistance` is the point where the volume reaches zero and the sound becomes inaudible.   
  
[AudioRolloffMode.Custom](AudioRolloffMode.Custom.html "AudioRolloffMode.Custom.html"): For the custom rolloff mode, the `maxDistance` sets the distance bounds of the curve. Any distance beyond holds the last available value.  
  
[AudioRolloffMode.Logarithmic](AudioRolloffMode.Logarithmic.html "AudioRolloffMode.Logarithmic.html"): For the logarithmic rolloff mode, the audio source ignores this setting. The sound will continue to attenuate with distance indefinitely.

[Switch to Manual](../Manual/class-ParticleSystem.html "Go to ParticleSystem Component in the Manual")

public bool alignToDirection;

### Description

Align particles based on their initial direction of travel.

The Shape Module supports setting the initial rotation of particles based on their direction of travel. This can be useful to make particles appear to have originated from the surface of a Mesh (for example, paint flaking off a surface). This works with any shape type. Unity applies any [ParticleSystem.startRotation](ParticleSystem-startRotation.html "ParticleSystem-startRotation.html") on top of this setting, so you can use both together.  
  
You can use this setting in conjunction with the [ParticleSystem.MainModule.startRotation](ParticleSystem.MainModule-startRotation.html "ParticleSystem.MainModule-startRotation.html") setting; Unity adds the rotation given by [ParticleSystem.MainModule.startRotation](ParticleSystem.MainModule-startRotation.html "ParticleSystem.MainModule-startRotation.html") on top of the value that [ParticleSystem.ShapeModule.alignToDirection](ParticleSystem.ShapeModule-alignToDirection.html "ParticleSystem.ShapeModule-alignToDirection.html") calculates.  
  
For example: add a [ParticleSystem.MainModule.startRotation](ParticleSystem.MainModule-startRotation.html "ParticleSystem.MainModule-startRotation.html") of 90 degrees when using [ParticleSystem.ShapeModule.alignToDirection](ParticleSystem.ShapeModule-alignToDirection.html "ParticleSystem.ShapeModule-alignToDirection.html"), and all the particles become perpendicular to the surface, like little spikes sticking out of it.

```
using UnityEngine;
using System.Collections;  
  
[RequireComponent(typeof(ParticleSystem))]
public class ExampleClass : MonoBehaviour
{
    private ParticleSystem ps;
    public bool toggle = true;  
  
    void Start()
    {
        ps = GetComponent<ParticleSystem>();
    }  
  
    void Update()
    {
        var shape = ps.shape;
        shape.alignToDirection = toggle;
    }  
  
    void OnGUI()
    {
        toggle = GUI.Toggle(new Rect(25, 45, 200, 30), toggle, "Align To Direction");
    }
}
```

public bool visible;

### Description

Indicates whether or not this element should be rendered.

The value of this property reflects the value of [IResolvedStyle.visibility](UIElements.IResolvedStyle-visibility.html "UIElements.IResolvedStyle-visibility.html") for this element.
The value is true for [Visibility.Visible](UIElements.Visibility.Visible.html "UIElements.Visibility.Visible.html") and false for [Visibility.Hidden](UIElements.Visibility.Hidden.html "UIElements.Visibility.Hidden.html").
Writing to this property writes to [IStyle.visibility](UIElements.IStyle-visibility.html "UIElements.IStyle-visibility.html").  
  
 Invisible elements are ignored by pointer events and by [IPanel.Pick](UIElements.IPanel.Pick.html "UIElements.IPanel.Pick.html").
  
  
Additional resources: [VisualElement.resolvedStyle](UIElements.VisualElement-resolvedStyle.html "UIElements.VisualElement-resolvedStyle.html"), [VisualElement.style](UIElements.VisualElement-style.html "UIElements.VisualElement-style.html")

### Description

A by-reference wrapper around something sent from [ControlContext.SendMessage](Audio.ControlContext.SendMessage.html "Audio.ControlContext.SendMessage.html").

Since this has no defined type, you will need to test with [ProcessorInstance.Message.Is](Audio.ProcessorInstance.Message.Is.html "Audio.ProcessorInstance.Message.Is.html") to discern between different
message types being delivered to you.

### Public Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Get](Audio.ProcessorInstance.Message.Get.html "Audio.ProcessorInstance.Message.Get.html") | Return a reference to the inner piece of data. You can modify this and the effects will be visible to the original message sender. |
| [Is](Audio.ProcessorInstance.Message.Is.html "Audio.ProcessorInstance.Message.Is.html") | Test whether this Message is of T. |

Suggestion\*


Submit suggestion

### Description

Combine the GameObject's Mesh with other eligible Meshes, to potentially reduce runtime rendering costs.

For more information, see the documentation on [Static Batching](../Manual/DrawCallBatching.html "../Manual/DrawCallBatching.html").  
  
Note that you can use [StaticBatchingUtility.Combine](StaticBatchingUtility.Combine.html "StaticBatchingUtility.Combine.html") to combine Meshes that do not have this StaticEditorFlag enabled at runtime.

```
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEditor;
public class StaticEditorFlagsExample
{
    [MenuItem("Examples/Create GameObject and set Static Editor Flags")]
    static void CreateGameObjectAndSetStaticEditorFlags()
    {
        // Create a GameObject
        var go = new GameObject("Example");
        // Set the GameObject's StaticEditorFlags
        var flags = StaticEditorFlags.BatchingStatic;
        GameObjectUtility.SetStaticEditorFlags(go, flags);
    }
}
```

Additional resources: [GameObjectUtility.SetStaticEditorFlags](GameObjectUtility.SetStaticEditorFlags.html "GameObjectUtility.SetStaticEditorFlags.html"), [GameObject.isStatic](GameObject-isStatic.html "GameObject-isStatic.html"), [StaticBatchingUtility.Combine](StaticBatchingUtility.Combine.html "StaticBatchingUtility.Combine.html")

public float magnitude;

### Description

Returns the length of this vector (Read Only).

The length of the vector is square root of `(x*x+y*y+z*z)`.  
  
If you only need to compare magnitudes of some vectors, you can compare squared magnitudes of them
using [sqrMagnitude](Vector3-sqrMagnitude.html "Vector3-sqrMagnitude.html") (computing squared magnitudes is faster).  
  
Additional resources: [sqrMagnitude](Vector3-sqrMagnitude.html "Vector3-sqrMagnitude.html").

## Declaration

public [Graph](Unity.GraphToolkit.Editor.Graph.html "Unity.GraphToolkit.Editor.Graph.html") GetSubgraph();

### Returns

**Graph**
The [Graph](Unity.GraphToolkit.Editor.Graph.html "Unity.GraphToolkit.Editor.Graph.html") instance that this node references.

### Description

Retrieves the subgraph linked to this node.

Call this method to access the subgraph that provides the behavior for this node.
The subgraph defines input and output variables that appear as ports on the subgraph node.
This method does not create or modify the subgraph.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| metadata | Additional contextual data for the marker |

### Description

Helper IDisposable struct for use with [ProfilerMarker.Auto](Unity.Profiling.ProfilerMarker.Auto.html "Unity.Profiling.ProfilerMarker.Auto.html").

Use [ProfilerMarker.Auto](Unity.Profiling.ProfilerMarker.Auto.html "Unity.Profiling.ProfilerMarker.Auto.html") to enclose a piece of code you want to profile in *using* statement. Constructor of *AutoScope* calls [ProfilerMarker.Begin](Unity.Profiling.ProfilerMarker.Begin.html "Unity.Profiling.ProfilerMarker.Begin.html") and *Dispose* method - [ProfilerMarker.Begin](Unity.Profiling.ProfilerMarker.Begin.html "Unity.Profiling.ProfilerMarker.Begin.html").

```
using Unity.Profiling;  
  
public class MySystemClass
{
    ProfilerMarker simulatePerfMarker = new ProfilerMarker("MySystem.Simulate");  
  
    public void UpdateLogic()
    {
        using (simulatePerfMarker.Auto())
        {
            // ...
        }
    }
}
```

## Declaration

public static [UnityWebRequest](Networking.UnityWebRequest.html "Networking.UnityWebRequest.html") Delete(string uri);

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| uri | The URI to which a `DELETE` request should be sent. |

### Returns

**UnityWebRequest**
A UnityWebRequest configured to send an HTTP `DELETE` request.

### Description

Creates a UnityWebRequest configured for HTTP `DELETE`.

This method creates a UnityWebRequest, sets the verb to `DELETE` and sets the target URL to the string argument `uri`. It sets no custom flags or headers.  
  
This method attaches no [DownloadHandler](Networking.DownloadHandler.html "Networking.DownloadHandler.html") or [UploadHandler](Networking.UploadHandler.html "Networking.UploadHandler.html") to the [UnityWebRequest](Networking.UnityWebRequest.html "Networking.UnityWebRequest.html").

## Declaration

public static bool BakeAsync();

### Returns

**bool**
Returns true if the bake was successfully started. Will return false and print a warning message if it's not possible to start the bake.

### Description

Starts an asynchronous bake job.

The progress can be monitored via [isRunning](Lightmapping-isRunning.html "Lightmapping-isRunning.html") property. [bakeStarted](Lightmapping-bakeStarted.html "Lightmapping-bakeStarted.html") will be called when the bake starts, and [bakeCompleted](Lightmapping-bakeCompleted.html "Lightmapping-bakeCompleted.html") when it is done.  
Only works in [Lightmapping.GIWorkflowMode.OnDemand](Lightmapping.GIWorkflowMode.OnDemand.html "Lightmapping.GIWorkflowMode.OnDemand.html") mode.   
  
If `-quit` is included in the command-line arguments, this method falls back to the synchronous [Lightmapping.Bake](Lightmapping.Bake.html "Lightmapping.Bake.html"). To quit the application after an asynchronous bake, use [Lightmapping.bakeCompleted](Lightmapping-bakeCompleted.html "Lightmapping-bakeCompleted.html") instead (for example, by calling `Application.Quit`).  
  
For synchronous bakes see [Bake](Lightmapping.Bake.html "Lightmapping.Bake.html").

### Description

Represents options for search filter operators. A colon (:) is the "contains" operator. A "-" is a "not" operator.

### Properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Equal](Unity.Hierarchy.HierarchySearchFilterOperator.Equal.html "Unity.Hierarchy.HierarchySearchFilterOperator.Equal.html") | Checks if a filter value is equal to the right-hand operand. |
| [Contains](Unity.Hierarchy.HierarchySearchFilterOperator.Contains.html "Unity.Hierarchy.HierarchySearchFilterOperator.Contains.html") | Checks if a filter value occurs within the right-hand operand. For instance, with a string value Contains uses string.Contains. |
| [Greater](Unity.Hierarchy.HierarchySearchFilterOperator.Greater.html "Unity.Hierarchy.HierarchySearchFilterOperator.Greater.html") | Checks if a numerical filter value is greater than the right-hand operand. |
| [GreaterOrEqual](Unity.Hierarchy.HierarchySearchFilterOperator.GreaterOrEqual.html "Unity.Hierarchy.HierarchySearchFilterOperator.GreaterOrEqual.html") | Checks if a numerical filter value is greater than or equal to the right-hand operand. |
| [Lesser](Unity.Hierarchy.HierarchySearchFilterOperator.Lesser.html "Unity.Hierarchy.HierarchySearchFilterOperator.Lesser.html") | Checks if a numerical filter value is less than the right-hand operand. |
| [LesserOrEqual](Unity.Hierarchy.HierarchySearchFilterOperator.LesserOrEqual.html "Unity.Hierarchy.HierarchySearchFilterOperator.LesserOrEqual.html") | Checks if a numerical filter value is less than or equal to the right-hand operand. |
| [NotEqual](Unity.Hierarchy.HierarchySearchFilterOperator.NotEqual.html "Unity.Hierarchy.HierarchySearchFilterOperator.NotEqual.html") | Checks if a filter value is different than the right-hand operand. |
| [Not](Unity.Hierarchy.HierarchySearchFilterOperator.Not.html "Unity.Hierarchy.HierarchySearchFilterOperator.Not.html") | Checks for items that do not match the filter value. |

### Description

Render texture color pixels are memoryless when [RenderTexture.antiAliasing](RenderTexture-antiAliasing.html "RenderTexture-antiAliasing.html") is set to 1.

Note that memoryless render textures are only supported on iOS/tvOS 10.0+ Metal and Vulkan. Render textures are read/write protected and stored in CPU or GPU memory on other platforms.  
  
Additional resources: [RenderTexture.memorylessMode](RenderTexture-memorylessMode.html "RenderTexture-memorylessMode.html"), [RenderTexture](RenderTexture.html "RenderTexture.html").

public float radius;

### Description

Returns or specifies the radius of the capsule bounding volume.

A negative value will automatically be converted into a positive value. If only a single radius axis is enabled, the value will automatically be converted to `0`. This value can never exceed half the [height](IMGUI.Controls.CapsuleBoundsHandle-height.html "IMGUI.Controls.CapsuleBoundsHandle-height.html").  
  
Additional resources: [PrimitiveBoundsHandle.axes](IMGUI.Controls.PrimitiveBoundsHandle-axes.html "IMGUI.Controls.PrimitiveBoundsHandle-axes.html").

public [Quaternion](Quaternion.html "Quaternion.html") inertiaTensorRotation;

### Description

The rotation of the inertia tensor.

If you don't set inertia tensor rotation from a script it will be calculated automatically from all colliders attached to the rigidbody.

```
// Resets the inertia tensor to be the coordinate system of the transform  
  
using UnityEngine;
using System.Collections;  
  
public class ExampleClass : MonoBehaviour
{
    void ResetTensor()
    {
        GetComponent<Rigidbody>().inertiaTensorRotation = Quaternion.identity;
    }
}
```

## Declaration

public static int clamp(int valueToClamp,
int lowerBound,
int upperBound);

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| valueToClamp | Input value to be clamped. |
| lowerBound | Lower bound of the interval. |
| upperBound | Upper bound of the interval. |

### Returns

**int**
The clamping of the input valueToClamp into the interval (inclusive) [lowerBound, upperBound].

### Description

Returns the result of clamping the value valueToClamp into the interval (inclusive) [lowerBound, upperBound], where valueToClamp, lowerBound and upperBound are int values.

## Declaration

public void SendLayoutChanged([AccessibilityNode](Accessibility.AccessibilityNode.html "Accessibility.AccessibilityNode.html") nodeToFocus);

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| nodeToFocus | An optional node to be focused by the screen reader after processing the notification. If a node is not provided and the currently focused node still exists, the screen reader does not change its focus. |

### Description

Notifies the screen reader that the layout of the screen changed and optionally requests it to move its
focus to a given accessibility node.

Call this method to notify the screen reader of minor adjustments to the user interface (for example,
when a dropdown is opened or closed), or to update the screen reader focus as a result of such changes
(for example, to move it off an accessibility node that may have been removed or deactivated so that the
screen reader's focus indicator isn't stuck on a stale node).
  
  
Calling this method prompts the screen reader to invalidate its cache of the accessibility hierarchy.
  
  
**Note**: On Windows and macOS, duplicate calls with the same argument are ignored by the screen reader.

protected bool needsApplyRevert;

### Description

Whether the ApplyRevertGUI method is required to draw in the Inspector.

Most Importers expose settings that are changed by users and require the Apply/Revert button to be pressed to update settings changes.
Some Importers, such as MonoScriptImporter, do not expose settings and do not require the use of the ApplyRevertGUI method to update changes.
In the cases where ApplyRevertGUI is not required, you can override needApplyRevert to return false. This avoids unnecessary checks on assets that the Importer Inspector performs when it is closed.

### Static Properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [currentViewWidth](EditorGUIUtility-currentViewWidth.html "EditorGUIUtility-currentViewWidth.html") | The width of the GUI area for the current EditorWindow or other view. This Property should only be accessed within an OnGUI call. |
| [editingTextField](EditorGUIUtility-editingTextField.html "EditorGUIUtility-editingTextField.html") | Is a text field currently editing text? |
| [fieldWidth](EditorGUIUtility-fieldWidth.html "EditorGUIUtility-fieldWidth.html") | The minimum width in pixels reserved for the fields of Editor GUI controls. |
| [hierarchyMode](EditorGUIUtility-hierarchyMode.html "EditorGUIUtility-hierarchyMode.html") | Is the Editor GUI in hierarchy mode? |
| [isProSkin](EditorGUIUtility-isProSkin.html "EditorGUIUtility-isProSkin.html") | Is the user currently using the pro skin? (Read Only) |
| [labelWidth](EditorGUIUtility-labelWidth.html "EditorGUIUtility-labelWidth.html") | The width in pixels reserved for labels of Editor GUI controls. |
| [pixelsPerPoint](EditorGUIUtility-pixelsPerPoint.html "EditorGUIUtility-pixelsPerPoint.html") | The scale of GUI points relative to screen pixels for the current viewThis value is the number of screen pixels per point of interface space. For instance, 2.0 on retina displays. Note that the value may differ from one view to the next if the views are on monitors with different UI scales. |
| [singleLineHeight](EditorGUIUtility-singleLineHeight.html "EditorGUIUtility-singleLineHeight.html") | Get the height used for a single Editor control such as a one-line EditorGUI.TextField or EditorGUI.Popup. |
| [standardVerticalSpacing](EditorGUIUtility-standardVerticalSpacing.html "EditorGUIUtility-standardVerticalSpacing.html") | Get the height used by default for vertical spacing between controls. |
| [systemCopyBuffer](EditorGUIUtility-systemCopyBuffer.html "EditorGUIUtility-systemCopyBuffer.html") | The system copy buffer. |
| [textFieldHasSelection](EditorGUIUtility-textFieldHasSelection.html "EditorGUIUtility-textFieldHasSelection.html") | True if a text field currently has focused and the text in it is selected. |
| [whiteTexture](EditorGUIUtility-whiteTexture.html "EditorGUIUtility-whiteTexture.html") | Get a white texture. |
| [wideMode](EditorGUIUtility-wideMode.html "EditorGUIUtility-wideMode.html") | Is the Editor GUI currently in wide mode? |

[Switch to Manual](../Manual/class-LightmapParameters.html "Go to LightmapParameters Component in the Manual")

public float pushoff;

### Description

The distance to offset the ray origin from the geometry when performing ray tracing, in modelling units. Unity applies the offset to all baked lighting: direct lighting, indirect lighting, environment lighting and ambient occlusion.

Changing the value of the offset can fix unwanted artifacts on faraway geometry that are the result of limited floating point precision. These artifacts resemble incorrect ambient occlusion or shadowing.  
  
The range of valid values is 0.0 - 1.0, inclusive.

### Description

The external reference clock the [VideoPlayer](Video.VideoPlayer.html "Video.VideoPlayer.html") observes to detect and correct drift.

The VideoPlayer plays the video based on an external time source. External time sources include your own custom timers, or a system’s time. To set this, use [VideoPlayer.externalReferenceTime](Video.VideoPlayer-externalReferenceTime.html "Video.VideoPlayer-externalReferenceTime.html").

[Switch to Manual](../Manual/class-MonoBehaviour.html "Go to MonoBehaviour Component in the Manual")

### Description

Called when the renderer becomes visible to any camera.

This message is sent to all scripts attached to the renderer. `OnBecameVisible` and [MonoBehaviour.OnBecameInvisible](MonoBehaviour.OnBecameInvisible.html "MonoBehaviour.OnBecameInvisible.html") are useful to avoid computations that are only necessary when the object is visible.  
  
The Scene view camera in the Unity Editor is treated like a regular camera for visibility checks, so `OnBecameVisible` can be called when objects are visible in the Scene view, even if the application isn't running. Scripts that execute in Edit mode can check [Application.isPlaying](Application-isPlaying.html "Application-isPlaying.html") before running important logic in `OnBecameVisible` to avoid unintended behavior in the Editor.  
  
`OnBecameVisible` can be a [coroutine](../Manual/Coroutines.html "../Manual/Coroutines.html").

```
// Enables the behaviour when it is visible  
  
using UnityEngine;
using System.Collections;  
  
public class ExampleClass : MonoBehaviour
{
    void OnBecameVisible()
    {
        enabled = true;
    }
}
```

[Switch to Manual](../Manual/class-PackageManager.html "Go to PackageManager Component in the Manual")

### Description

Skip the Asset Database refresh that normally runs after the sample's files are imported.

Use this when chaining multiple imports or performing additional setup work in a [Sample.OnBeforeImportFinish](PackageManager.UI.Sample.OnBeforeImportFinish.html "PackageManager.UI.Sample.OnBeforeImportFinish.html") handler, so the refresh runs once after all work completes rather than after each individual import. When set, the caller is responsible for triggering an Asset Database refresh when the imported files should be picked up.

### Description

Script interface for texture mipmap limit groups.

Use this class to add, remove or detect texture mipmap limit groups in C#.  
  
Additional resources: [TextureMipmapLimitSettings](TextureMipmapLimitSettings.html "TextureMipmapLimitSettings.html"), [QualitySettings.globalTextureMipmapLimit](QualitySettings-globalTextureMipmapLimit.html "QualitySettings-globalTextureMipmapLimit.html").

### Static Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [CreateGroup](TextureMipmapLimitGroups.CreateGroup.html "TextureMipmapLimitGroups.CreateGroup.html") | (Editor Only) Attempts to create a texture mipmap limit group with the indicated groupName. |
| [GetGroups](TextureMipmapLimitGroups.GetGroups.html "TextureMipmapLimitGroups.GetGroups.html") | Retrieves a string array containing the name of all texture mipmap limit groups available in the project. |
| [HasGroup](TextureMipmapLimitGroups.HasGroup.html "TextureMipmapLimitGroups.HasGroup.html") | Checks whether a texture mipmap limit group with the indicated groupName exists in the project. This operation fails and throws an exception if groupName is null. |
| [RemoveGroup](TextureMipmapLimitGroups.RemoveGroup.html "TextureMipmapLimitGroups.RemoveGroup.html") | (Editor Only) Attempts to remove a texture mipmap limit group with the indicated groupName. |

public bool enableTightPacking;

### Description

Determines if sprites should be packed tightly during packing.

Tight packing means the mesh of the sprite is used as the boundary of the sprite during packing, instead of the full rectangle.

public string[] downloadFailedAssetPacks;

### Description

Gets the names of Android asset packs that failed to download.

The Android asset pack names this property returns correspond to asset pack downloads that either failed due to some error or that the end user canceled. For more information, call [AndroidAssetPacks.DownloadAssetPackAsync](Android.AndroidAssetPacks.DownloadAssetPackAsync.html "Android.AndroidAssetPacks.DownloadAssetPackAsync.html") and pass a callback method to it. Unity raises the callback with additional information, such as the error code, during the download.
Note: This list also includes the names of Android asset packs for which Google's PlayCore API did not raise any callbacks. This happens if you access this property right away after calling DownloadAssetPackAsync, before the PlayCore API raises any of the callbacks.
Read-only.
Additional resources: DownloadAssetPackAsyncOperation.isDone [[DownloadAssetPackAsyncOperation.progress.

public static bool compressionEnabled;

### Description

Controls compression of cache data. Enabled by default.

If cache compression is enabled, then all data will be stored in a compressed form using fast LZ4 algorithm.
This property affects only further downloads. It doesn't compress or decompress existing content in the cache.  
  
Default value is "true".  
  
Additional resources: [UnityWebRequestAssetBundle.GetAssetBundle](Networking.UnityWebRequestAssetBundle.GetAssetBundle.html "Networking.UnityWebRequestAssetBundle.GetAssetBundle.html").

### Description

Indicates that the operating system's language is Serbo-Croatian.

```
using UnityEngine;  
  
public class Example : MonoBehaviour
{
    void Start()
    {
        //This checks if your computer's operating system is in the Serbo-Croatian language
        if (Application.systemLanguage == SystemLanguage.SerboCroatian)
        {
            //Outputs into console that the system is Serbo-Croatian
            Debug.Log("This system is in Serbo-Croatian. ");
        }
    }
}
```

### Description

Applies forces to attract/repulse against a point.

When the source [Collider2D](Collider2D.html "Collider2D.html") is a trigger, the effector will apply forces whenever the target [Collider2D](Collider2D.html "Collider2D.html") overlaps the source. When the source [Collider](Collider.html "Collider.html") isn't a trigger, the effector will apply forces whenever the target [Collider2D](Collider2D.html "Collider2D.html") is in contact with the source only.  
  
This effector is designed primarily to work with source [Collider2D](Collider2D.html "Collider2D.html") that are set as triggers so that target [Collider2D](Collider2D.html "Collider2D.html") can overlap the defined area.

### Properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [angularDamping](PointEffector2D-angularDamping.html "PointEffector2D-angularDamping.html") | The angular damping to apply to rigid-bodies. |
| [distanceScale](PointEffector2D-distanceScale.html "PointEffector2D-distanceScale.html") | The scale applied to the calculated distance between source and target. |
| [forceMagnitude](PointEffector2D-forceMagnitude.html "PointEffector2D-forceMagnitude.html") | The magnitude of the force to be applied. |
| [forceMode](PointEffector2D-forceMode.html "PointEffector2D-forceMode.html") | The mode used to apply the effector force. |
| [forceSource](PointEffector2D-forceSource.html "PointEffector2D-forceSource.html") | The source which is used to calculate the centroid point of the effector. The distance from the target is defined from this point. |
| [forceTarget](PointEffector2D-forceTarget.html "PointEffector2D-forceTarget.html") | The target for where the effector applies any force. |
| [forceVariation](PointEffector2D-forceVariation.html "PointEffector2D-forceVariation.html") | The variation of the magnitude of the force to be applied. |
| [linearDamping](PointEffector2D-linearDamping.html "PointEffector2D-linearDamping.html") | The linear damping to apply to rigid-bodies. |

public int compressionQuality;

### Description

The quality of the texture after Crunch compresses it. The range is 0 through 100. A higher value means a larger, better-quality texture, but a longer compression time because Crunch needs more time to try different texture encodings.

This will only affect the default platform setting. Additional resources: [TextureImporterPlatformSettings](TextureImporterPlatformSettings.html "TextureImporterPlatformSettings.html"), [TextureCompressionQuality](TextureCompressionQuality.html "TextureCompressionQuality.html"), [TextureImporter.SetPlatformTextureSettings](TextureImporter.SetPlatformTextureSettings.html "TextureImporter.SetPlatformTextureSettings.html").

## Declaration

public static void PushCamera([Camera](Camera.html "Camera.html") camera);

### Description

Store all camera settings.

The camera settings will be added to a so-called "stack" list, where they will stay until retrieved by a call to [PopCamera](HandleUtility.PopCamera.html "HandleUtility.PopCamera.html"). The settings will be stored in the reverse of the order in which they were added, so a call to PopCamera will retrieve the most recently stored Camera data and then remove it from the stack. A subsequent call to PopCamera will then retrieve the next most recently pushed data and so on.

## Declaration

public int GetVertexBufferStride(int stream);

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| stream | Vertex data stream index to check for. |

### Returns

**int**
Vertex data size in bytes in this stream, or zero if the stream is not present.

### Description

Get vertex buffer stream stride in bytes.

This method returns the stride of a vertex buffer stream, specified by `stream` index. The stride is the total size in bytes occupied by all vertex attributes belonging to a single vertex within that specific stream. It represents the distance in bytes between the beginning of one vertex's data and the beginning of the next vertex's data in the buffer associated with that stream.  
  
You need the stride value when performing calculations for direct buffer access (e.g., using [MeshData](Mesh.MeshData.html "Mesh.MeshData.html") or [GraphicsBuffer](Mesh.GraphicsBuffer.html "Mesh.GraphicsBuffer.html")) or when interfacing with graphics APIs that require vertex buffer layout information. For example, you can use the stride to calculate the memory address of a specific vertex within the stream's buffer `address = baseAddress + vertexIndex * stride`.  
  
Note: the stride gives the total size of a vertex within the stream, not the offset of a specific attribute within that vertex. To get the offset of a particular attribute within its stream, use [GetVertexAttributeOffset](Mesh.GetVertexAttributeOffset.html "Mesh.GetVertexAttributeOffset.html").

```
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEngine.Rendering;  
  
public class ExampleScript : MonoBehaviour
{
    void Start()
    {
        // Create a Mesh with custom vertex data layout:
        // position and normal go into stream 0,
        // color goes into stream 1.
        var mesh = new Mesh();
        mesh.SetVertexBufferParams(10,
            new VertexAttributeDescriptor(VertexAttribute.Position, VertexAttributeFormat.Float32, 3, stream:0),
            new VertexAttributeDescriptor(VertexAttribute.Normal, VertexAttributeFormat.Float32, 3, stream:0),
            new VertexAttributeDescriptor(VertexAttribute.Color, VertexAttributeFormat.UNorm8, 4, stream:1));  
  
        // Prints 2 (two vertex streams)
        Debug.Log($"Vertex stream count: {mesh.vertexBufferCount}");
        // Next two lines print: 24 (12 bytes position + 12 bytes normal), 4 (4 bytes color)
        Debug.Log($"Steam 0 stride {mesh.GetVertexBufferStride(0)}");
        Debug.Log($"Steam 1 stride {mesh.GetVertexBufferStride(1)}");  
  
        // Cleanup
        Object.DestroyImmediate(mesh);
    }
}
```

Additional resources: [vertexBufferCount](Mesh-vertexBufferCount.html "Mesh-vertexBufferCount.html"), [GetVertexAttributeOffset](Mesh.GetVertexAttributeOffset.html "Mesh.GetVertexAttributeOffset.html"), [SetVertexBufferParams](Mesh.SetVertexBufferParams.html "Mesh.SetVertexBufferParams.html").

public [FilterMode](LightingSettings.FilterMode.html "LightingSettings.FilterMode.html") filteringMode;

### Description

Specifies the filter type that the Progressive Lightmapper uses for ambient occlusion. (Editor only).

When this is set to None, the Progressive Lightmapper does not filter ambient occlusion. When this is set to any other value, the Progressive Lightmapper filters the computed ambient occlusion with the specified filter.  
  
This setting affects lightmaps generated by the Baked Global Illumination system. It only applies to the the Progressive Lightmapper.  
  
When Unity serializes this `LightingSettings` object as a [Lighting Settings Asset](../Manual/class-LightingSettings.html "../Manual/class-LightingSettings.html"), this property corresponds to the **Filtering > Ambient Occlusion** property in the Lighting Settings Asset Inspector.  
  
Additional resources: [Lighting Settings Asset](../Manual/class-LightingSettings.html "../Manual/class-LightingSettings.html").

### Description

Import textures with texture compression off.

You can set [EditorUserBuildSettings.overrideTextureCompression](EditorUserBuildSettings-overrideTextureCompression.html "EditorUserBuildSettings-overrideTextureCompression.html") to `ForceUncompressed` to import
all textures into uncompressed texture formats. This is the same as if all the textures had "Compression: None"
option set in their import settings.  
  
This setting is mostly useful for local development, to speed up texture importing or a platform
switch process. Some compressed texture formats are slow to compress, and for local development
you might want to skip that. Note however that uncompressed textures do take up more memory
and might be slower for GPU to render with.  
  
Additional resources: [EditorUserBuildSettings.overrideTextureCompression](EditorUserBuildSettings-overrideTextureCompression.html "EditorUserBuildSettings-overrideTextureCompression.html"), [Texture Importer](../Manual/class-TextureImporter.html "../Manual/class-TextureImporter.html"), [command line arguments](../Manual/CommandLineArguments.html "../Manual/CommandLineArguments.html").

public float offsetDistance;

### Description

Vertices are offset by this distance when compositing multiple physic shapes. Any vertices between shapes within this distance are combined.

Do not set the distance offset to higher than 1% of the Sprite's length, as this may result in a loss in detail when too many vertices are combined together.

public [CullingOptions](Rendering.CullingOptions.html "Rendering.CullingOptions.html") cullingOptions;

### Description

Flags to configure a culling operation in the Scriptable Render Pipeline.

Unity sets some of the [CullingOptions](Rendering.CullingOptions.html "Rendering.CullingOptions.html") flags with default values, and others depending on the properties of the [Camera](Camera.html "Camera.html") from which you obtained the [ScriptableCullingParameters](Rendering.ScriptableCullingParameters.html "Rendering.ScriptableCullingParameters.html") struct. You can override these values before performing the culling operation.  
  
The following example demonstrates how to retrieve a ScriptableCullingParameters object from a Camera, disable occlusion culling on the ScriptableCullingParameters object by unsetting the CullingOptions.OcclusionCull flag, and then use the ScriptableCullingParameters object in a culling operation.

```
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEngine.Rendering;  
  
public class ExampleRenderPipelineInstance : RenderPipeline
{
    public ExampleRenderPipelineInstance()
    {
    }  
  
    protected override void Render(ScriptableRenderContext context, Camera[] cameras)
    {
        // Get the culling parameters from the desired Camera
        if (cameras[0].TryGetCullingParameters(out var cullingParameters))
        {
            // Disable occlusion culling
            cullingParameters.cullingOptions &= ~CullingOptions.OcclusionCull;  
  
            // Schedule the cull operation
            CullingResults cullingResults = context.Cull(ref cullingParameters);  
  
            // Place code that schedules drawing operations using the CullingResults struct here
            // See ScriptableRenderContext.DrawRenderers for details and examples
            // …  
  
            // Execute all of the scheduled operations, in order
            context.Submit();
        }
    }
}
```

[Switch to Manual](../Manual/class-Camera.html "Go to Camera Component in the Manual")

### Description

[Event function](../Manual/event-functions.html "../Manual/event-functions.html") that Unity calls before a Camera culls the scene.

In the Built-in Render Pipeline, Unity calls `OnPreCull` on MonoBehaviours that are attached to the same GameObject as an enabled Camera component, just before performing the culling operation that determines what that Camera can see. For a full description and code example, see [MonoBehaviour.OnPreCull](MonoBehaviour.OnPreCull.html "MonoBehaviour.OnPreCull.html").  
  
For similar functionality that does not require the script to be on the same GameObject as a Camera component, see [Camera.onPreCull](Camera-onPreCull.html "Camera-onPreCull.html").  
  
If you're using a Scriptable Render Pipeline, for example the Universal Render Pipeline, use Rendering.RenderPipelineManager instead.
